public_rationale: The evidence does not settle the claim on its ordinary contextual reading. OpenAI acknowledged remaining unsafe behavior in GPT-4. Pre-post research also offered genuine guarantees for bounded prompt attacks and specified robot constraints. Those results deserve consideration, but their existence alone does not establish meaningful assurance that generative AI systems behave safely in their intended use. Conversely, GPT-4's failures and an unsuccessful search for broader assurance do not prove that nobody had engineered it. A supported or contradicted verdict would exceed the records examined.
limitations: This assessment concerns achievements by February 21, 2024, not subsequent progress.
The available evidence covers selected systems and methods, not every historical engineering effort.
The wording leaves the required breadth of a safety guarantee unspecified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No one has ever been able to engineer safety guarantees for generative AI systems.

statement.excerpt: Nobody has ever been able to engineer safety guarantees around then.

our_interpretation: Read “then” as a typographical error for “them,” referring to the generative AI systems discussed in the post.
The plain reading is that nobody had engineered meaningful assurance that these systems would behave safely in their intended use by February 21, 2024.

A qualifying guarantee must address the safety of the functioning system within a stated operating scope. Reasonable operating assumptions are acceptable; freedom from every conceivable harm is not required.
A certificate for one attack mechanism or component does not by itself establish the system-level assurance described in the claim. Its coverage and assumptions must be examined.
“Ever” covers the history preceding publication, so the target period has no specified starting date. This is not a forecast that safety guarantees will remain impossible.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive technical assessment of the field as it stood by February 21, 2024 establishes that meaningful system-level safety assurance had not been engineered, addressing credible candidate systems and the limitations of their guarantees.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented system engineered by February 21, 2024 demonstrably provides meaningful assurance of safe behavior in its intended operating scope, with justified assumptions and coverage of the relevant hazards. An isolated conditional certificate is insufficient without evidence connecting it to that assurance.

evidence.explanation: The proposed safety module enforces human-verified formal constraints around an LLM-driven robot, making it a more relevant candidate than a prompt certificate alone. Its assurance assumes perfect state predicates and a transition model; the examined evidence does not establish coverage of the hazards needed for the broader assurance meant here.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented pre-post system with verified safety assurance covering its intended use and justified operating assumptions would contradict the claim. A comprehensive historical technical assessment addressing credible candidates and establishing that such assurance remained unavailable would support it.
